correctness.rationale: Exact Poisson mixing gives log G=λ(∏(1+p_i(z_i−1))−1)+Σφ_i(z_i−1), so distinct-index derivatives give μ_i=λp_i+φ_i, C_ij=λp_ip_j, T=λp_1p_2p_3. Substitution reconstructs all seven parameters and proves necessity and sufficiency of the moment inequalities. The two-visit pairs yield the same full PGF. The scaling family preserves all means and covariances but changes the triple moment. 3456 exact rational shock decompositions and the two-visit equality were independently checked with the packaged script; finite tests do not replace proof.

value.rationale: Spurious count detections are a motivated obstacle in unmarked automated ecological abundance surveys. The claim yields a natural exact classification: three occasions and one third cross-moment separate latent abundance from all unknown visit-specific background rates, two complete visits provably cannot, and only pair moments cannot at any visit count. The explicit inequalities characterize all realizable seven-moment summaries and enable model feasibility screening. It is not merely a renamed textbook statistic or arbitrary finite census, and it makes no finite-sample performance promises.
